shared_context.topic: stopping Prozac due to side effects
shared_context.condition: side effects and discontinuation of an SSRI

atoms.1: Abrupt discontinuation of Prozac is not recommended.
atoms.2: Abrupt discontinuation of fluoxetine is not recommended.
atoms.3: Prozac is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI).
atoms.4: Fluoxetine is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI).
atoms.5: Abrupt discontinuation of SSRIs can lead to withdrawal symptoms.
atoms.6: Gradual tapering of SSRIs is generally advised.
atoms.7: Gradual tapering of Prozac is generally advised.
atoms.8: Gradual tapering of fluoxetine is generally advised.
atoms.9: Gradual tapering is advised to minimize withdrawal symptoms.
atoms.15: Medications that affect the central nervous system should be tapered off under the guidance of a healthcare provider.
atoms.16: SSRIs should be tapered off under the guidance of a healthcare provider.
atoms.17: Tapering off SSRIs under the guidance of a healthcare provider can help avoid withdrawal symptoms.

snippets.output: Abrupt discontinuation of Prozac (fluoxetine), a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI), is not recommended due to the potential for withdrawal symptoms.
Gradual tapering of SSRIs, including Prozac (fluoxetine), is generally advised to minimize withdrawal symptoms.
Withdrawal symptoms from SSRIs can include dizziness, nausea, headache, irritability, and insomnia.
Medications that affect the central nervous system, such as SSRIs, should be tapered off under the guidance of a healthcare provider to avoid withdrawal symptoms.
